title: 2 Samuel Chapter 9 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Samuel chapter 9 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 9 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Samuel Chapter 9.

questions.question: Who did David ask if there was anyone left from the house of Saul to show kindness to?
questions.correctAnswer: Jonathan
questions.explanation: David asked if there was anyone left of the house of Saul to show kindness for Jonathan's sake, as stated in 2 Samuel 9:1.

questions.question: What was the name of the servant from the house of Saul who was called to David?
questions.correctAnswer: Ziba
questions.explanation: The servant of the house of Saul called to David was named Ziba, according to 2 Samuel 9:2.

questions.question: True or False: David asked Ziba if Jonathan had a son who was lame on his feet.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: David inquired if Jonathan had a son who was lame, as Ziba informed him, in 2 Samuel 9:3.

questions.question: Where was Jonathan's son said to be living?
questions.correctAnswer: Lodebar
questions.explanation: Ziba told David that Jonathan's son was in the house of Machir in Lodebar, as recorded in 2 Samuel 9:4.

questions.question: Who was Machir, in relation to the place where Jonathan's son lived?
questions.correctAnswer: Son of Ammiel
questions.explanation: The text states that Jonathan's son was in the house of Machir, son of Ammiel, in Lodebar (2 Samuel 9:4).

questions.question: What action did King David take regarding Jonathan's son?
questions.correctAnswer: He sent for him
questions.explanation: King David sent and fetched Jonathan's son from the house of Machir, as stated in 2 Samuel 9:5.

questions.question: True or False: Mephibosheth was Jonathan's son and was lame on both feet.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Mephibosheth, son of Jonathan, was lame on his feet as mentioned in 2 Samuel 9:6 and 2 Samuel 9:13.

questions.question: What did Mephibosheth do when he came before King David?
options: Fell on his face and did reverence
questions.correctAnswer: Fell on his face and did reverence
questions.explanation: When Mephibosheth came to David, he fell on his face and did reverence, as described in 2 Samuel 9:6.

questions.question: True or False: David promised to restore all the land of Saul to Mephibosheth and let him eat at his table continually.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: David promised Mephibosheth all the land of Saul and that he would eat at the king's table continually (2 Samuel 9:7).

questions.question: How did Mephibosheth describe himself when David showed him kindness?
questions.correctAnswer: A dead dog
questions.explanation: Mephibosheth humbly called himself a 'dead dog' when David showed him kindness (2 Samuel 9:8).

questions.question: What did David instruct Ziba to do regarding the land given to Mephibosheth?
options: To till the land and bring in the fruits for Mephibosheth
To give the land to the people
questions.correctAnswer: To till the land and bring in the fruits for Mephibosheth
questions.explanation: David told Ziba to till the land and bring in the fruits so Mephibosheth would have food (2 Samuel 9:10).

questions.question: Who ate bread continually at King David's table?
questions.correctAnswer: Mephibosheth
questions.explanation: Mephibosheth was to eat bread continually at the king's table as noted in 2 Samuel 9:7 and 2 Samuel 9:10.

questions.question: How many sons did Ziba have who would help till the land for Mephibosheth?
questions.explanation: Ziba had fifteen sons who would till the land for Mephibosheth, as stated in 2 Samuel 9:10.

questions.question: Who was Mephibosheth's young son?
questions.correctAnswer: Micha
questions.explanation: Mephibosheth had a young son named Micha, according to 2 Samuel 9:12.

questions.question: True or False: All who dwelt in the house of Ziba were servants to Mephibosheth.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The chapter states that all who dwelt in Ziba's house were servants to Mephibosheth (2 Samuel 9:12).

medium.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 9 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Samuel Chapter 9 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who was Mephibosheth in relation to Saul?
questions.correctAnswer: Jonathan's son
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 9:6 clearly states Mephibosheth is the son of Jonathan, who was Saul's son, linking him directly to Saul's house.

questions.question: What promise did David make to Mephibosheth regarding Saul's land?
options: He would restore all the land of Saul to him
He would give him a new kingdom
He would sell Saul's land to him
He would share the land with Ziba
questions.correctAnswer: He would restore all the land of Saul to him
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 9:7, David promises to restore all the land of Saul to Mephibosheth for Jonathan's sake.

questions.question: How did Mephibosheth respond to David's kindness?
options: He humbled himself, calling himself a dead dog
questions.correctAnswer: He humbled himself, calling himself a dead dog
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 9:8 describes Mephibosheth bowing and referring to himself as a 'dead dog' to express humility before the king.

questions.question: What task was assigned to Ziba and his family in relation to Mephibosheth's land?
options: To till the land and bring in the fruits for Mephibosheth
To guard the land from enemies
To live on the land with Mephibosheth
To sell the land and give the money to Mephibosheth
questions.correctAnswer: To till the land and bring in the fruits for Mephibosheth
questions.explanation: According to 2 Samuel 9:10, Ziba, his sons, and servants were to work the land and bring in its produce so Mephibosheth would have food.

questions.question: What does 2 Samuel 9:11 teach us about obedience and faithfulness through Ziba's response?
options: Ziba pledges to obey all the king’s commands faithfully
Ziba refuses to till the land
questions.correctAnswer: Ziba pledges to obey all the king’s commands faithfully
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 9:11, Ziba agrees to do whatever the king commands, demonstrating faithful obedience and trust in the king's authority.

questions.question: What does the fact that Mephibosheth ate continually at the king's table symbolize about David's kindness?
options: Inclusion and honor as one of the king's sons
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusion and honor as one of the king's sons
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 9:7 and 9:11 explain that Mephibosheth would eat at David’s table continually, symbolizing his acceptance and honor like a royal son.

questions.question: What does David’s treatment of Mephibosheth teach about forgiveness and grace?
options: David shows kindness despite Mephibosheth’s disability and family history
David punishes Mephibosheth for Saul's sins
questions.correctAnswer: David shows kindness despite Mephibosheth’s disability and family history
questions.explanation: David’s actions in 2 Samuel 9:6-7 show grace and forgiveness by restoring honor and land to Mephibosheth despite his physical disability and Saul’s troubled history.

questions.question: True or False: Mephibosheth was lame on both his feet.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 9:13 states explicitly that Mephibosheth was lame on both his feet, confirming the truth of this statement.

questions.question: Based on 2 Samuel 9:7 and 9:10, what does the passage teach about the importance of generosity in leadership?
options: Leaders should provide for those in need as David provided for Mephibosheth
Leaders should withhold resources to maintain power
Leaders should only reward their immediate family
Leaders should expect payment for help given
questions.correctAnswer: Leaders should provide for those in need as David provided for Mephibosheth
questions.explanation: David’s restoration of Saul’s land and provision of food at his table (2 Samuel 9:7, 9:10) teaches that generosity and care are essential qualities in godly leadership.

questions.question: What does 2 Samuel 9:9-10 suggest about the relationship between Mephibosheth and Ziba after David's declaration?
options: Ziba and his family were assigned to serve Mephibosheth by working the land
Mephibosheth was made servant to Ziba
Ziba was exiled from the land
Mephibosheth and Ziba shared the land equally
questions.correctAnswer: Ziba and his family were assigned to serve Mephibosheth by working the land
questions.explanation: David assigned Ziba, his sons, and servants to till the land and provide food for Mephibosheth (2 Samuel 9:9-10), establishing a servant-master relationship.

questions.question: How does Mephibosheth’s humility in 2 Samuel 9:8 teach us about responding to undeserved kindness?
options: We should respond with humility and recognize our unworthiness
We should boast about the kindness received
questions.correctAnswer: We should respond with humility and recognize our unworthiness
questions.explanation: Mephibosheth’s self-description as a 'dead dog' in 2 Samuel 9:8 exemplifies humble acceptance of kindness, recognizing that such favor is undeserved.

questions.question: True or False: David restored Mephibosheth to his former status because of his own merit and achievements.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: David restored Mephibosheth not for Mephibosheth's merit but for Jonathan's sake, as stated in 2 Samuel 9:1 and 9:7, showing kindness based on covenant loyalty.

questions.question: What does the number of Ziba's family members working the land suggest about the provision for Mephibosheth?
options: There was a large labor force to ensure Mephibosheth was well provided for
Ziba’s family was too small to care for the land
Mephibosheth had to work the land himself
questions.correctAnswer: There was a large labor force to ensure Mephibosheth was well provided for
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 9:10 mentions Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants, indicating a substantial workforce to produce food for Mephibosheth.

questions.question: True or False: Mephibosheth had a son named Micha who also lived in Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 9:12 states Mephibosheth had a young son named Micha, and those dwelling in Ziba's house were servants to Mephibosheth, implying family presence in Jerusalem.

questions.question: What does 2 Samuel 9:7 promise will happen if the reader trusts in David’s kindness as shown to Mephibosheth?
options: They will receive restoration and continual provision
They will be exiled from the kingdom
They must prove their worth by working the land
questions.correctAnswer: They will receive restoration and continual provision
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 9:7 shows David promising restoration of land and continual provision at his table for Mephibosheth, teaching that faith in God's kindness brings restoration.

hard.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 9 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Samuel Chapter 9.

questions.question: What commitment did King David make regarding Mephibosheth's status at his table?
options: He shall eat at the king's table as one of the king's sons
He shall serve as a servant in the palace
He shall receive a portion of the land but not eat at the table
He shall be sent to live in exile
questions.correctAnswer: He shall eat at the king's table as one of the king's sons
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 9:11 states David's promise that Mephibosheth would eat at his table as one of the king's sons, showing David's kindness and honor toward him.

questions.question: Who was Micha in relation to Mephibosheth?
questions.correctAnswer: His young son
questions.explanation: According to 2 Samuel 9:12, Micha was the young son of Mephibosheth, establishing Mephibosheth's family lineage.

questions.question: What role did those dwelling in the house of Ziba have in relation to Mephibosheth?
options: They were fellow heirs to Saul's land
questions.correctAnswer: They were servants to Mephibosheth
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 9:12 explains that all who dwelt in Ziba's house were servants to Mephibosheth, indicating the transfer of authority and household status.

questions.question: Where did Mephibosheth live after King David's kindness was shown to him?
questions.correctAnswer: In Jerusalem
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 9:13 states that Mephibosheth dwelt in Jerusalem and ate continually at the king's table, symbolizing his restored status.

questions.question: What physical condition did Mephibosheth have?
options: He was lame on both his feet
questions.correctAnswer: He was lame on both his feet
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 9:13 notes that Mephibosheth was lame on both his feet, a fact mentioned earlier in 2 Samuel 9:3 and 9:4, indicating his physical disability.

questions.question: What was the cultural significance of David inviting Mephibosheth to eat at his table continually?
options: It symbolized full acceptance and restoration to the royal family
It meant Mephibosheth was now a servant
It was a customary gesture to all guests
It implied Mephibosheth would inherit the throne
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolized full acceptance and restoration to the royal family
questions.explanation: In ancient Near Eastern culture, eating at a king’s table signified honor, acceptance, and restoration, as seen in 2 Samuel 9:7 and 2 Samuel 9:13.

questions.question: How does the kindness David shows to Mephibosheth foreshadow New Testament themes?
options: It prefigures Christ's grace and inclusion of the marginalized
It predicts the division of the kingdom
It foreshadows the exile to Babylon
It echoes the giving of the Law
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures Christ's grace and inclusion of the marginalized
questions.explanation: David’s kindness to the disabled and marginalized Mephibosheth (2 Samuel 9:7-13) parallels New Testament themes of grace and restoration through Christ (e.g., Luke 14:12-14).

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage similarly emphasizes showing kindness for the sake of a covenant relationship?
questions.correctAnswer: Genesis 24:12-14
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:12-14 highlights Abraham’s servant seeking kindness for his master’s family, paralleling David’s kindness to Saul’s house in 2 Samuel 9:1-7.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the name 'Mephibosheth' and its significance in this chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Dispeller of shame
questions.explanation: The name 'Mephibosheth' means 'dispeller of shame' or 'exterminator of shame' in Hebrew, which is significant as David restores his honor and status (2 Samuel 9:6-13).

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in this chapter to highlight the theme of restoration?
options: Inclusio framing the narrative by mentioning kindness at the start and end
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio framing the narrative by mentioning kindness at the start and end
questions.explanation: The chapter uses inclusio by starting (9:1) and ending (9:13) with kindness, framing Mephibosheth’s restoration and highlighting the theme of mercy.

questions.question: Which historical context helps explain David’s motive to show kindness to Saul’s house?
options: To honor his covenant with Jonathan and stabilize his reign
To eliminate all threats to his kingdom
To fulfill a prophecy of exile
questions.correctAnswer: To honor his covenant with Jonathan and stabilize his reign
questions.explanation: David’s kindness to Saul’s house honors his covenant with Jonathan (2 Samuel 9:1-7) and serves political purposes by securing loyalty and legitimacy.

questions.question: What does Ziba’s response to David’s command reveal about his role?
options: He accepts his role to serve Mephibosheth faithfully
He refuses to obey the king
He requests more land for himself
questions.correctAnswer: He accepts his role to serve Mephibosheth faithfully
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 9:11 shows Ziba affirming he will obey David’s commands and serve Mephibosheth, demonstrating loyalty and fulfilling duties.

questions.question: True or False: Mephibosheth was reluctant to approach King David because he feared retribution for Saul’s house.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Mephibosheth’s humble words in 2 Samuel 9:8 reveal his fear and low self-esteem, indicating reluctance to approach the king due to his family’s downfall.

questions.question: True or False: Ziba had no sons or servants to tend the land for Mephibosheth.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 9:10 states that Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants to till the land for Mephibosheth, showing a well-established household.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of restoring honor to the disabled and marginalized as seen in this chapter?
questions.explanation: Luke 14:12-14 emphasizes inviting the poor and disabled to feast, paralleling David’s kindness to Mephibosheth (2 Samuel 9:7,13).

theological.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 9 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Samuel Chapter 9 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is primarily demonstrated by David's initial inquiry about any surviving member of Saul's house to show kindness for Jonathan's sake?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 9:1 reveals David's intent to show kindness (mercy) toward Saul's house for Jonathan's sake, highlighting God's mercy extended through David.

questions.question: Who was identified as the servant of Saul's house that informed David about Jonathan's son?
questions.correctAnswer: Ziba
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 9:2 identifies Ziba as Saul's servant who was called to David and confirmed his identity.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 9:3, what condition did Jonathan's son have?
questions.correctAnswer: Lame on his feet
questions.explanation: Ziba informs David in 2 Samuel 9:3 that Jonathan's son is lame on his feet, specifying his physical disability.

questions.question: Where was Mephibosheth living before David summoned him?
options: In the house of Machir at Lodebar
questions.correctAnswer: In the house of Machir at Lodebar
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 9:4 states Mephibosheth was residing in Machir's house in Lodebar before David sent for him.

questions.question: What does Mephibosheth's act of falling on his face before David signify in a theological context?
questions.correctAnswer: Reverence and submission
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 9:6 shows Mephibosheth's posture as reverence and submission to David’s kingly authority, reflecting humility before God's appointed ruler.

questions.question: What promise did David make to Mephibosheth illustrating God's covenantal faithfulness?
options: Restore all Saul's land and continual provision at his table
Make him king instead of David
questions.correctAnswer: Restore all Saul's land and continual provision at his table
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 9:7 records David promising to restore Saul’s land to Mephibosheth and provide for him at the king’s table continually, demonstrating God's covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: How does Mephibosheth's self-description as a 'dead dog' reflect biblical anthropology about human worth apart from God's grace?
options: It shows humility and low self-worth
questions.correctAnswer: It shows humility and low self-worth
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 9:8, Mephibosheth calls himself a 'dead dog,' a metaphor for lowly and unworthy status, illustrating human humility before God’s grace.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by David giving Saul's land to Mephibosheth and appointing Ziba and his household to work it?
questions.correctAnswer: Providence and stewardship
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 9:9-10 shows God's providential care in providing for Mephibosheth through stewardship and labor by Ziba's household to sustain him.

questions.question: What does the presence of fifteen sons and twenty servants in Ziba's household indicate about the socio-economic structure of Saul's former servants?
options: A large retinue maintained for service
A priestly family dedicated to temple work
questions.correctAnswer: A large retinue maintained for service
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 9:10 mentions Ziba's extensive household, indicating a large retinue maintained for serving Mephibosheth and managing Saul's land.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 9:11, how does David's directive about Mephibosheth eating at the king's table reflect the doctrine of union with the king?
options: It symbolizes inclusion into the royal family
It forbids Mephibosheth from royal privileges
It isolates him from God's people
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes inclusion into the royal family
questions.explanation: David's command in 2 Samuel 9:11 for Mephibosheth to eat at the king's table symbolizes his inclusion into the royal family, reflecting union with the king's covenant blessings.

questions.question: What is the significance of Mephibosheth having a son named Micha in the context of covenant continuation?
options: It signifies the continuation of Saul's line
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies the continuation of Saul's line
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 9:12 mentions Mephibosheth's son Micha, demonstrating the ongoing fulfillment of God's covenant promises through Saul's descendants.

questions.question: How does Mephibosheth’s residence in Jerusalem and continual eating at the king's table foreshadow the spiritual blessings believers receive in Christ?
options: It prefigures believers' fellowship with Christ as King
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures believers' fellowship with Christ as King
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 9:13 shows Mephibosheth dwelling in Jerusalem and eating at the king's table, foreshadowing believers' intimate fellowship with Christ, the King, in God's presence.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that showing kindness to an enemy's family is politically motivated rather than a reflection of divine character. What does 2 Samuel 9:1–7 teach about God's character through David's actions?
options: God's covenantal mercy motivates kindness beyond politics
Kindness is purely strategic and lacks divine basis
David acted selfishly without regard for God's character
God endorses political manipulation over mercy
questions.correctAnswer: God's covenantal mercy motivates kindness beyond politics
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 9:1–7 shows David acting out of covenant faithfulness to Jonathan, demonstrating God's merciful character that transcends politics (cf. Romans 5:8).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth about God's grace and human disability is taught by 2 Samuel 9:3 and 2 Samuel 9:13?
options: Grace includes restoration and honor despite physical weakness
Disability disqualifies one from God's blessings
Physical perfection is required for divine favor
God's grace is only for the physically strong
questions.correctAnswer: Grace includes restoration and honor despite physical weakness
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 9:3 notes Mephibosheth's lameness, and 9:13 shows his honored place at the king's table, teaching God's grace restores and honors despite human weakness.

questions.question: How do verses 9 and 10 together illustrate the doctrine of stewardship and provision in God's kingdom?
options: God provides through human agents for the needy
Laborers are excluded from God's provision
questions.correctAnswer: God provides through human agents for the needy
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 9:9-10 shows David assigning Ziba and his household to work the land for Mephibosheth’s benefit, illustrating God’s provision through stewardship.
